parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Version the system people actually use
parts.body:
A production AI system changes when its data, model, prompt, retrieval settings, tools, policy, or user workflow changes. A model name alone cannot reproduce an answer. Keep a release manifest that binds the model and version, prompt or instruction configuration, data or index snapshot, embedding and reranking settings, tool versions and permissions, evaluation suite, and application code. Record which population received the release and when. Some hosted models change behind a service label; contracts and telemetry should make the extent of reproducibility clear.

MLOps covers the lifecycle of data and trained models; LLMOps adds prompt, retrieval, tool, and often provider configuration to the artifacts under test. Google Cloud's MLOps guidance describes automated testing, release, deployment, and monitoring throughout an ML system. For an enterprise CAIO, the operational question is whether the team can compare a candidate with the current configuration, explain a failure, and return to a known acceptable state.

Assign owners. The product team owns task quality and user workflow; a platform team owns deployment and shared telemetry; data owners approve sources; security and privacy owners set control requirements. A release can require evidence from each without giving everyone a vague collective veto. Use a registry and change log the on-call team can inspect during an incident, not only a slide presented at launch.

example.title: One manifest entry
example.body: Release 1.8 includes model route B, prompt revision 12, index snapshot dated 6 May, retrieval top-k of five, policy bundle 4, application build 203, and evaluation suite 7. The dates and versions are illustrative; the point is to bind all inputs that could change an answer.

exercise.title: Create a manifest
exercise.body: For an assistant you know, list every artifact needed to reproduce a response and who can change it. Mark any provider behavior you cannot pin and the telemetry or contractual term you need to detect a change.

sources: Google Cloud: MLOps continuous delivery and monitoring
NIST AI RMF Core: documentation and monitoring

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Evaluate before exposing a release
parts.body:
Choose test cases that represent real tasks, difficult edge cases, and consequential failures. An internal knowledge assistant needs questions with current source answers, conflicting documents, missing evidence, and users with different permissions. An action-taking agent also needs tests for tool authorization, repeated actions, and recovery after a failed step. Grade factual support, completeness, harmful omission, abstention, latency, and cost where relevant. Human reviewers should inspect a sample because an automated grader may share a model's blind spots.

Compare a candidate release with the current one on the same cases and a fresh sample. Define thresholds in advance, including a maximum for severe errors even if the average rises. Evaluate the whole application path, not only a raw model response; an index or permission change can alter results while the model is unchanged. Keep the exact cases and scoring rules with the release record. Test new regional content and populations before expanding coverage.

Use a staged deployment. Shadow traffic can reveal behavior without showing answers to users, provided the data use is authorized. A small canary then tests actual latency, adoption, corrections, and incidents. A named release owner reviews results and stops expansion when a guardrail is breached. NIST's AI RMF Measure function emphasizes documented evaluation methods and testing in context; no single benchmark proves the application is ready for every workflow.

example.title: A release that fails despite an average gain
example.body: A new retrieval setting improves correct answers from 82% to 86% on a hypothetical test set but exposes two restricted passages. The pre-agreed severe-error limit is zero, so the team blocks release and fixes authorization before considering the average gain.

exercise.title: Build a 12-case suite
exercise.body: Write six routine, three exception, two permission, and one missing-source case for a chosen assistant. Give each an expected behavior and severity. Set release thresholds, a human review sample, and a canary stop condition.

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Monitor outcomes and diagnose drift
parts.body:
Production monitoring should answer whether the system still helps in the intended context. Track task outcome and human corrections alongside technical signals such as error rate, latency, token or compute spend, retrieval misses, and tool failures. Sample output quality using privacy-aware methods. Segment by task type, region, and user population when those differences matter. A stable uptime chart can coexist with answers that grew stale after a policy update.

Set an owner and response for each alert. A sudden cost rise may call for a route limit or a budget change; a severe unauthorized disclosure calls for containment, investigation, and the organization's incident process. Monitor source freshness and access revocations as well as model behavior. Review model or vendor updates, changes in the business process, and seasonal shifts that may alter the case mix. Feedback from workers is a signal to investigate, not a substitute for a measured sample.

Use thresholds that connect to action. A weekly quality sample falling below the agreed minimum triggers review or rollback; a data correction can trigger targeted regression tests. Record the affected release and population so the team can find possibly impacted outputs. NIST's Manage function calls for responses to mapped and measured risks; the operating runbook should say who can pause the feature and how the business continues while it is paused.

example.title: A stale policy incident
example.body: After a benefits policy update, cited answers still point to an old version in one region. The on-call team disables that topic, restores a manual search path, updates the index, tests affected cases, and identifies prior answers needing review.

exercise.title: Write four runbook lines
exercise.body: For a cost spike, quality drop, permission leak, and provider outage, state the signal, threshold, incident owner, containment action, user fallback, and evidence required to resume.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Manage and monitoring

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Plan rollback and recovery
parts.body:
A rollback plan must cover every artifact that shaped the failed behavior. If a new embedding configuration lowers answer quality, switching only the language model will not restore the earlier retrieval index. Preserve the last acceptable model route, prompt, index snapshot, tool policy, application build, and evaluation result. Define the signal that triggers rollback, the person authorized to act, the order of changes, and the test that confirms recovery. Some changes, such as a customer-facing answer already sent, cannot be undone by software rollback and need a communication or correction process.

Test the rollback path before launch. Restore a prior index in a rehearsal, run known cases, verify permissions, and measure how long the process takes. Keep a manual route for essential work during an outage. If the old configuration carries a separate security flaw, rolling back blindly could worsen the incident; the incident lead may instead disable the affected feature while a fix is prepared. Document that choice and its business impact.

Ask executives to fund operating readiness in the same decision as launch. On-call support, retained snapshots, evaluation maintenance, and incident communication cost money. The CAIO should see whether promised value still survives those costs and whether owners can meet the recovery objective. An application that no one can safely pause or restore is not ready to scale.

example.title: An embedding rollback
example.body: A candidate index reduces cited-answer accuracy below the pilot threshold. The release owner returns traffic to the previous index and retrieval settings, reruns the permission and answer suite, checks a live sample, and logs the period and users exposed. If inaccurate customer answers were sent, the business owner reviews correction needs.

exercise.title: Rehearse one failure
exercise.body: Choose an index, prompt, tool, or model change. Write the detection threshold, rollback authority, exact prior artifacts, maximum tolerable interruption, regression test, manual fallback, and plan for reviewing outputs already delivered.
